en: The man who is walking is good.
explain: _quī_ starts a clause that describes _vir_. It is masculine singular because _vir_ is, and nominative because it is the one walking.
distractors: _quae_ is feminine (or neuter plural). _vir_ is masculine: _quī_.
_quem_ is accusative. The one walking is the subject: _quī_.

en: The girl who is walking is good.
explain: _quae_ agrees with _puella_ (feminine) and is nominative: she is the one walking.
distractors: _quam_ is accusative. The one walking is the subject: _quae_.

en: The thing that I see is good.
explain: _id_ is “that thing”; _quod_ is the neuter “which”. I see it, so it is accusative, and neuter nominative and accusative look the same.

en: The man whom I see is good.
explain: The relative takes its gender from _vir_ (masculine) and its case from its own clause: I see him, so accusative _quem_.
distractors: _quī_ is nominative. Inside the clause the man is seen, so accusative: _quem_.

en: The girl whom I see is good.
explain: Feminine from _puella_, accusative because I see her: _quam_.
distractors: _quae_ is nominative. Inside the clause she is seen, so accusative: _quam_.

en: The men who are walking are good.
explain: Masculine plural nominative is _quī_, the same spelling as the singular. The plural verb _ambulant_ shows it is plural.
distractors: _quōs_ is accusative. The ones walking are the subject: _quī_.
_quem_ is singular accusative. The ones walking are plural subjects: _quī_.

en: The men whom I see are good.
explain: Masculine plural, and accusative because I see them: _quōs_.
distractors: _quī_ is nominative. Inside the clause the men are seen, so accusative: _quōs_.

en: The women whom I see are good.
explain: Feminine plural, accusative because I see them: _quās_.
distractors: _quae_ is nominative. Inside the clause the women are seen, so accusative: _quās_.

en: The things that I see are good.
explain: _ea_ is “those things”; _quae_ is the neuter plural “which”. Neuter plural nominative and accusative are the same.

en: This is the man whom I love.
explain: Same rule: _vir_ is masculine singular, and in the clause I love him, so accusative: _quem_.
distractors: _quī_ is nominative. In the clause he is loved, so accusative: _quem_.
